title: Hidden Quantum Geometry in Bilayer Exciton Condensates
abstract: When an electron-doped layer is stacked with a hole-doped layer with approximately equal carrier density, inter-layer Coulomb interaction turns the bilayer system into an exciton condensate (EC). In this Letter, we reveal a fundamental property of bilayer ECs: the excitonic order gives rise to nontrivial hidden quantum geometric effects in the correlated electron-hole bands, even when the non-interacting bands are trivial. Such peculiar EC-driven quantum geometry manifests itself in a characteristic out-of-plane polarization response upon applying an in-plane AC electric field to the bilayer EC system. In particular, the second-order response exhibits a characteristic inverse square scaling with the bilayer EC order parameter. Our finding reveals a fundamental hidden Berry phase effect driven by electron-hole correlations, and establishes bilayer EC as a promising platform for rich nonlinear physics.
summary: This theoretical work investigates how the formation of an exciton condensate in bilayer materials induces hidden quantum geometry. By calculating the second-order polarization response ($\chi^{(2)}$) to an external electric field, the authors predict a unique signature: that this nonlinear response scales inversely with the square of the excitonic order parameter ($\Delta^{-2}$). This establishes bilayer ECs as a platform for studying correlation-driven Berry phase effects.
main_problem: To determine if excitonic order itself generates intrinsic quantum geometry in a bilayer exciton condensate (EC), even when non-interacting bands are trivial.
main_result: The second-order dipole response function exhibits a characteristic inverse square power law dependence on the EC order parameter ($\chi^{(2)} \propto \Delta^{-2}$), revealing a hidden Berry phase effect driven by electron-hole correlations.
method: The study employs quantum kinetic equations, Wigner transformation to phase space, and perturbative expansion in $\hbar$ to calculate linear and second-order response functions.
model_or_system: A bilayer system formed by stacking electron-doped and hole-doped layers, which forms an exciton condensate (EC) due to inter-layer Coulomb interaction. The physics is analyzed using mean-field Hamiltonians and quasi-particle descriptions.
key_observables: Out-of-plane polarization ($P_z$), the second-order dipole response function ($\chi^{(2)}_{z;\alpha eta}$), and the hidden in-plane Berry curvature ($\Omega^n_{\alpha}(\mathbf{k})$).
important_parameters: The excitonic order parameter ($\Delta$), the external AC electric field ($\mathbf{E}(t)$), and the inverse square scaling dependence on $\Delta$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies heavily on semi-classical approximations via Wigner transformation, perturbative expansion in $\hbar$, and specific limits like long wavelength or small order parameter.
figures_summary: Not specified by notes; the focus is on deriving scaling laws ($\chi^{(2)} \propto 1/\Delta^2$) and functional forms for response functions.
paper_structure: The paper systematically develops a response theory, first establishing the Hamiltonian in phase space via Wigner transformation. It then calculates linear and second-order responses, culminating in the derivation of the $\chi^{(2)}$ scaling law based on excitonic coherence.
why_interesting: The explicit calculation of nonlinear optical responses ($\chi^{(2)}$) driven by emergent quantum geometric properties (Berry curvature) provides a concrete, measurable signature for correlated electron phenomena, linking fundamental theory to potential experimental detection in condensed matter systems.
